studio: Workflow -> Gallery — runs link their outputs (1.4.0 P1.2)

A finished workflow run writes a sidecar next to every file it produced
inside the plugin's workflow_outputs root: {workflow: {run_id, graph}}.
Existing sidecars (WanGP's own settings JSON) merge instead of being
replaced, and files outside the output root are never touched.

media_index.detail surfaces the workflow record, and the lightbox shows
'Graph name · run id' as a fact row — closing the loop from the 1.4.0
flagship scenario back to the Gallery.

Integration test: input_video(path) + ffmpeg_trim run through the real
run worker, sidecar verified on disk and through MediaIndex.detail;
helper is unit-tested to never touch files outside the output root.

studio: pending-media queue survives canvas activation races

activate() rebuilds the canvas frame from an empty literal, so media
nodes folded into state.graph were lost on the CI timing. addMediaInput
now queues requests until a frame exists and every buildFrame flushes
them after the srcdoc script installs its message listener.

studio: Media -> Workflow — gallery files land on the canvas (1.4.0 P1)

The flagship 1.4.0 scenario starts: a gallery file becomes a workflow
input node. The lightbox gains 'Use in workflow' (image/video/audio):
it switches to the canvas and adds an input_image/video/audio node with
the file path preset; the runner consumes params.path before the
runtime upload slots (fork commit 152ec52).

- vendored canvas gets its second documented patch: host push action
  'add_media' -> addMediaNode (mirrors the fork editor.js);
- workflow.js addMediaInput() pushes to a live canvas or folds the node
  into the graph buildFrame() will render; getGraph() exported for tests;
- e2e: gallery -> lightbox -> Use in workflow -> the canvas graph carries
  input_image with the corpus file path.

studio: soak clears filters before capturing its base total

The control-audit CI run exposed an order dependence: kind_filter_and_search
leaves 'prompt hint 3' in the search box, so the soak captured 400 as its
base and then waited forever for the unfiltered count to equal it. The soak
now clears the filter first, waits for the fetch queues to drain, and only
then captures the base.

studio: audit hardening from the 1.3.4 control review (1.3.5)

- upload history is bounded: finished entries beyond 100 leave the
  queue (and the DOM), and a successful upload releases the File
  reference; failed/cancelled entries keep it for retry;
- loadPage markers are generation-scoped tokens ("gen:page"): a stale
  request's finally can no longer un-mark the current request for the
  same page after a filter reset;
- e2e regression for the empty uploads panel visibility (the exact bug
  live acceptance caught) and an honest deep-scroll content check (the
  far end must actually show the oldest corpus file);
- new manual/weekly Media benchmark workflow runs the 10k perf tests
  (slim deps: pillow, psutil, pytest).

studio: stage-E soak test and gate env isolation

- e2e long-session soak: four deep scroll cycles, a full refresh,

ci: stub the thumbnail engine in e2e instead of chasing its dep chain

The preview import chain reaches rembg, whisper and more - installing
that universe into the e2e runner is a treadmill. The harness tests
gallery bounds, not preview rendering: sys.modules stub makes every
thumbnail request fail fast and deterministically (broken-image state),
the connection pool stays free, and the job keeps the slim dependency
set. test_thumbnail_bytes still covers the real engine where the chain
imports.

studio: Playwright e2e harness + gallery fixes it caught (1.3.4 stage D)

New e2e/ harness: a real uvicorn server with a 2800-file corpus driven
by headless Chromium (separate 'Studio E2E' workflow, Playwright
pinned). Five tests pin the frontend half of the scalability
criterion: page-store window stays bounded while scrolling to the far
end, evicted pages are refetched on scroll-back, the upload queue
drains with per-file status and refreshes the gallery, filters and
search answer.

Writing them caught and fixed three real gallery bugs:
- upload queue stall: finishUpload() never pumped the next queued
  file, so uploads beyond UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY sat queued forever;
- eviction raced with out-of-order responses: evicting relative to the
  fetched page could drop the page the user is looking at; eviction is
  now anchored to the viewport in render();
- renderUploadRows() assumed a cancel button exists on every row and
  threw on queued rows.

debug(): gallery exposes pages/fetching/cards counters as a test
contract. Waits in the e2e drive renders synchronously via the resize
handler (headless rAF is not guaranteed to pump between assertions).

Verified: e2e 5 passed twice locally; full suites 223 passed.

studio: bounded gallery memory, upload center, strict GPU gate (1.3.4)

Stage A - CI quality:
- WANFLOW_REQUIRE_CUDA=1 turns a missing GPU into a configuration error
  instead of a skip (the strict acceptance run refuses to hide the
  heavy modules);
- test_vendored_sync.py fails loudly when the vendored wanflow snapshot
  and the fork HEAD drift apart in either direction.

Stage B - Media Center memory:
- gallery keeps only KEEP_PAGES pages around the viewport; evicted
  pages render as skeletons and are refetched on scroll-back, so
  state.items no longer grows without limit during long sessions;
- selection capped at 1000 ids;
- the 10k benchmark now measures cold scan (0.40s), incremental reuse
  (4 ms), one changed directory (42 ms), reconcile (0.39s), query
  variants (22-45 ms) and backend RSS (65 -> 76 MB).

Stage C - Upload Center:
- drop/browse uploads run as a bounded-parallelism queue (2 concurrent)
  with per-file XHR progress, failure reasons, retry, cancel and a
  gallery refresh once the queue drains.

ci: trigger on vendored wanflow changes, surface skip reasons

- the path filters never included plugins/wan2gp-wanflow-ui/**, so a
  commit touching only the vendored plugin (graph_runner, cuda_gate,
  its tests) would not run the suite at all; the last green run only

- synced from the plugin repo: test_cuda_exclusions.py reports each of
  the six CUDA-dependent modules as an explicit named skip on CPU-only
  runners and a collection confirmation on GPU machines
